prompt: CHALLENGE: The Sharpless asymmetric epoxidation uses Ti(OiPr)₄, (CH₃)₃COOH, and a chiral DET ((+) or (−)-diethyl tartrate) to convert an allylic alcohol into a chiral epoxide. What determines which enantiomer forms?

options.label: The chirality of DET (D vs L / + vs −). (+)-DET gives one epoxide enantiomer; (−)-DET gives the other. The chiral Ti complex delivers oxygen to a specific face of the alkene.

explanation: Sharpless' Nobel-winning method only works on allylic alcohols — the OH coordinates to Ti, directing the oxygen delivery face. The DET enantiomer dictates which face. Predictable rule: with the allylic alcohol drawn with OH down and alkene to the right, (−)-DET gives O above the plane, (+)-DET gives O below.
